server_list_contracts.notes: zod-validated page/limit (limit max 100), offset computed, count(*) total query, orderBy createdAt desc. Admin-only (requireAdmin). No local .vue in apps/web calls this directly — consumed by the legacy template layer's own admin UI (not visible in this app's source without install), so the pagination UI itself is NOT a float-forecast-local reimplementation, but the contract shape is good evidence for the shared table's server-side pagination design.

top_extraction_candidates.name: River detail tile-grid family
top_extraction_candidates.why: Four separate hand-rolled tile-grid components (Stats/ForecastBring/RouteLogistics/SafetyAlerts, 38-70 LOC each) share the same tile-grid shape and would collapse into one KPI/stat-tile primitive with per-item slots.

top_extraction_candidates.name: Server-side page/limit list contract
top_extraction_candidates.why: Already-proven { items/total/page/limit } shape (via the legacy layer's admin UI) is good precedent evidence for the shared table's server contract, even though float-forecast itself has no local UI consuming it.

notes: Consumer-facing river-guide app: no literal tables/pagination/sort UI anywhere (grep for <UTable|<table|role=table returned zero hits) — all list-shaped data renders as card grids or tile grids, not rows. Two components (OutlookDayCard, OutlookErrorCard) and two grid components (ConsumerConditionGrid, RiverSpotCard) had zero production consumers found via tag search; flagged rather than asserted dead, since dynamic component resolution was not checked. The one real pagination CONTRACT in the repo (server/api/users.get.ts) has no local UI consumer — it feeds the legacy template layer's own admin panel.
